## What Is an Employer of Record in The Gambia


An Employer of Record (EOR) in The Gambia is a third-party company that becomes the legal employer of your workers under Gambian law. The EOR signs employment contracts, handles payroll, and manages compliance with the Labour Act 2023, while you keep full control over day-to-day work, performance, and project direction.


As[employment law in Gambia](https://www.lawgratis.com/blog-detail/employment-law-in-gambia) outlines, the Labour Act 2023 governs employment relations and requires written contracts for all non-casual employees covering salary, duties, working hours, and duration. An EOR handles all of that on your behalf, including Social Security and Housing Finance Corporation (SSHFC) contributions and PAYE tax filings.


For a foreign company, the practical benefit is straightforward. Registering a local entity in The Gambia takes time, legal fees, and ongoing compliance overhead. An EOR skips that entirely. You identify the person you want to hire, the[employer of record](https://www.bolto.com/employer-of-record) hires them locally as the legal employer, and you get to work.


## Employment Laws and Compliance Requirements in The Gambia


The Labour Act 2023 is the primary framework governing employment in The Gambia, covering contracts, leave, termination, and social security obligations. For foreign companies[hiring international workers](https://www.bolto.com/blog/hire-international-workers-guide-us-employers) directly, the compliance load is real and the penalties for missteps are enforced by the Department of Labour.


### Contracts and Probation


Under the Labour Act, written contracts are generally required for all non-casual employees and should be in place within seven days of commencement. They typically cover salary, duties, working hours, and contract duration. Probation periods generally run up to 90 days for general employees and up to 365 days for skilled workers.


### SSHFC and Payroll Tax


Under the Labour Act, new hires are generally registered with the Social Security and Housing Finance Corporation (SSHFC) within 14 days. The[SSHFC administers three schemes](https://www.sshfc.gm/overview) : the Federated Pension Fund (employer pays 15% of gross salary), the National Provident Fund (10% employer, 5% employee deduction), and the Industrial Injuries Compensation Fund (1% of gross salary, employer-paid). Pay As You Earn (PAYE) income tax applies to employment income on a progressive basis.


### Leave and Termination


Maternity leave is generally 14 weeks, typically paid after 12 months of service. Paid sick leave generally runs to 14 days per year. Termination typically requires written notice and a fair hearing. Severance is generally calculated at 2 months' basic pay for each year worked, including cases of the employee's death or business closure.

This is general information, not legal advice. Rules vary by situation and change over time, so consult a qualified employment lawyer for your specific circumstances.

## Cost of Hiring in The Gambia with an EOR vs. a Local Entity

The incorporation fee runs 6% of share capital (minimum roughly $143). Annual compliance adds another[$400 to $1,000 per year](https://www.playroll.com/compliance-hub/local-entity-required-to-hire-in-gambia) in corporate tax filings and reporting. Those fixed costs apply whether you have one employee or twenty.

## EOR vs. Local Entity in The Gambia: Which Is Right for You


The right structure depends on two factors: how many people you're hiring and how long you plan to stay.


### When an EOR Is the Right Choice


An EOR fits your situation in The Gambia when:


- You have no existing legal entity in The Gambia or West Africa and need a compliant path in without months of setup work.
- You're testing the market before committing to a permanent presence, keeping your options open if plans change.
- Headcount is small, typically one to a few employees, where entity overhead would far outweigh the benefit. Startups weighing their options on the[best EOR for startups](https://www.bolto.com/blog/what-is-the-best-eor-for-startups) often fall into exactly this scenario.
- Speed is a factor: EOR onboarding takes 48 hours, while setting up a local entity runs six to eight weeks at minimum.
- Compliance uncertainty is high across the Labour Act, SSHFC regulations, and GRA tax requirements.


### When a Local Entity May Make Sense


A local entity becomes worth considering when:


- You plan to operate long-term, sign local contracts, and own assets in The Gambia.
- You're hiring 50 or more employees, at which point per-employee EOR costs can outweigh entity overhead.
- You operate in an industry with licensing or registration requirements that mandate a direct local business presence.
- Long-term equity administration for Gambian team members is a priority.


For most companies hiring their first one to ten people in The Gambia, the fixed setup costs, ongoing compliance burden, and exit complexity of a local entity are difficult to make a case for. An EOR provides a compliant, scalable path in from day one, with the option to transition to a local entity if the business case eventually warrants it. Fast-growing companies can review the[best global EOR providers for startups](https://www.bolto.com/blog/best-global-eor-providers-for-startups) to find the right long-term fit.
